record.title: FIRE reports failure-derived runtime policies improve repeated agent task success
record.summary: An arXiv preprint studies runtime policies derived from observed agent failures: targeted instructions or action denials trigger at risky execution states without changing model weights or user prompts. The authors report a randomized five-arm Terminal-Bench panel in which their frozen policies improve success on eligible tasks over baseline and timing-matched sham, while generic verify and reconsider prompts do not reproduce the result. Across an 87-task subset of Terminal-Bench 2.1, the authors also report higher two-attempt success for three model tiers. These are author-reported findings: the prespecified panel policy-versus-sham estimate is +25.0 percentage points with a wide 95% interval [7.1, 46.4] and p=0.061; two tasks were excluded because pinned images could not install the agent. The evidence is limited to English terminal tasks and has no independent replication.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv preprint describes runtime policies derived from observed task failures, implemented as targeted instructions or action denials triggered by task and execution state without changing model weights or user prompts.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the authors’ randomized five-arm panel on 14 policy-eligible Terminal-Bench tasks, the frozen runtime policies pass 17/28 attempts (60.7%), compared with 10/28 (35.7%) for a timing-matched sham and 11/28 (39.3%) for baseline. The prespecified policy-versus-sham difference is +25.0 points with a 95% interval [7.1, 46.4] and p=0.061; the estimate is large but imprecise.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across the authors’ 87-task Terminal-Bench subset and two attempts per task, policy-guided repeated success rises from 50.6% to 54.0% for Luna, 55.2% to 60.9% for Terra, and 64.4% to 73.6% for Sol. The complete suite excludes two of the benchmark’s 89 tasks because their pinned images could not install the agent.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The authors report a benchmark-specific result from frozen policies and English terminal tasks; policies were derived from failures in the same research program. The paper provides no independent reproduction or evidence of transfer to other domains, harnesses, languages or production agents.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the frozen runtime-policy portfolio or five-arm comparison was located. Attempt-level paper results remain author-reported.
Transfer beyond English Terminal-Bench tasks, these models, this harness and policies derived from this research program is unmeasured.
Two of 89 Terminal-Bench tasks were omitted from complete-suite comparisons because their pinned images could not install the agent.

brief.importance_rationale: If independently reproduced and transferred, targeted runtime policies could improve dependable delivery of agent work without changing model weights, reducing the gap between capabilities an agent can reach and solutions it reliably delivers. Score 5 reflects a potentially useful engineering method supported by a controlled but small author-run study; it does not measure confidence and does not imply general production effectiveness.
limitations: All performance results are author-reported; no independent reproduction was located or performed.
The prespecified five-arm primary contrast has a wide interval and p=0.061; the 14 eligible tasks provide limited precision.
The two-attempt design measures observed repeatability but does not identify per-task success probabilities.
Complete-suite results cover 87 of 89 Terminal-Bench tasks after two image-installation exclusions.
Evaluation uses English terminal tasks, the authors’ selected models and harness, and policies derived from the same research program; external validity is unknown.
brief.summary: An arXiv preprint studies runtime policies derived from observed agent failures: targeted instructions or action denials trigger at risky execution states without changing model weights or user prompts. The authors report a randomized five-arm Terminal-Bench panel in which their frozen policies improve success on eligible tasks over baseline and timing-matched sham, while generic verify and reconsider prompts do not reproduce the result. Across an 87-task subset of Terminal-Bench 2.1, the authors also report higher two-attempt success for three model tiers. These are author-reported findings: the prespecified panel policy-versus-sham estimate is +25.0 percentage points with a wide 95% interval [7.1, 46.4] and p=0.061; two tasks were excluded because pinned images could not install the agent. The evidence is limited to English terminal tasks and has no independent replication.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report 17/28 passes (60.7%) for real policies on eligible tasks versus 10/28 (35.7%) for timing-matched sham and 11/28 (39.3%) for baseline. Primary difference vs sham is +25.0 points (95% CI [7.1,46.4], p=0.061). On all 87 tasks, pass^2 rises 50.6→54.0% Luna, 55.2→60.9% Terra and 64.4→73.6% Sol.
technical.compute_or_cost: The authors report policy-guided Terra reaching 71.4% against unassisted Sol at 64.3% on the 14-task frozen portfolio, at about half the cost. This comparison is author-reported and specific to selected tasks/models; complete lifecycle costs are not independently measured.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper directly describes its policy abstraction, frozen portfolio, randomized panel and metrics. Reported outcomes have not been independently checked against raw run artifacts or reproduced in this activation.
technical.implementation_status: Research preprint describes policies integrated into the authors’ agent harness. No independent implementation or replication was examined.
technical.mechanism: The authors derive policy eligibility and runtime triggers from observed failure states. At selected harness events, a policy adds a short instruction or denies a tool action; the frozen portfolio does not alter model weights or the user prompt.
technical.novelty: Derives targeted runtime interventions from observed procedural failures and tests policy content against same-event sham and generic self-checking controls, distinguishing reliable delivery from capability.
technical.regime: arXiv v1 submitted 2026-09-22. Terminal-Bench 2.1; 87 of 89 tasks in complete-suite analysis, two attempts per task, three author-selected GPT-5.6 tiers. Separate randomized five-arm panel: 14 eligible plus 16 silent tasks, five arms and two attempts per task/arm (300 attempts).
technical.reproducibility: No independent reproduction or audit of raw attempt artifacts was located or performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: For causal attribution, the authors’ timing-matched sham on the same eligible tasks is the primary comparator; generic always-verify and reconsider arms are secondary controls. The primary policy-versus-sham estimate is imprecise.

brief.title: FIRE reports failure-derived runtime policies improve repeated agent task success
brief.why_it_matters: If independently reproduced and transferred, harness policies tied to observable failure states could make agent solutions more dependable without retraining. The reported experiment offers a controlled but small, author-run result: its prespecified policy-versus-sham interval is wide, coverage is limited to English terminal tasks, and broad transfer is not established.
